children: shares decreased 1.62% at 10.35 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 17, a day after the Commerce Department issued a rule requiring licenses for advanced chip shipments to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil. The shares slid about 4% on Monday when the rule surfaced. Today's pause still leaves them well below the 52-week high of $658.52.

The interim final rule, scheduled for publication on November 19, also requires licenses for data centers anywhere that sell more than 12 million aggregate TPP of remote computing to China-headquartered companies. Law firm Nixon Peabody outlined a 90-day window for existing arrangements and an exemption for US-headquartered buyers whose exporters file monthly reports. Singapore accounted for 12.4% of AMD's 2025 revenue, the Motley Fool noted on Monday. Appaloosa Management sold all 197,500 of its AMD shares in the third quarter.

Revenue booked in Singapore may not match chips deployed there, so the 12.4% figure likely overstates the direct hit, but license reviews could slow shipments to regional cloud builders. GuruFocus gives AMD a GF Score of 81/100, with a strong balance sheet offset by a stretched valuation. The GF Value of $318.98 puts the shares at a 58% premium, which GuruFocus labels significantly overvalued, leaving little room for a guidance cut. The next test is how quickly licenses clear inside the 90-day window.

title: AMD Stocks Decrease 1.62% as New US Rule Requires Licenses for Five Chip Hubs
